_comment: C0-14 higgsfield bodies EN. 无附加小节。正文「相关条目」4 行带 .md 链接（runway/luma/kling/krea），related 写 4 条。sources 3 条对齐 frontmatter。

axes.model_access: Aggregation + in-house hybrid: the platform offers generation entries for multiple models (as seen in site navigation) + an in-house line (the company name doubles as the model-brand narrative). The concrete aggregation list has not been inventoried item by item.
axes.runtime: Web (higgsfield.ai); generation on the vendor's cloud. No official offline-weights line seen.
axes.local_files: Works stored account-side in the cloud, generation history visible on the web works page; downloads go local. No officially stated local data surface.
axes.background: Generation is instant/queued (varies by tier, not verified item by item); no "keep-running-after-shutdown" task surface (no claim verified).
axes.tools: **Camera Control (the Move series) is its signature differentiator** (the site's lead narrative: preset camera moves — dolly/crash zoom/crane etc., one-click application); image-to-video, effect-template lines (as seen in site navigation).
axes.context: Organized by account works; cross-session memory — no official statement verified. Camera-move presets are its "consistency" mechanism — reusable, not memory.
axes.permissions: Account + subscription system (D9: prices not collected); the training-use switch not verified line by line; commercial and watermark limits on free-tier output follow the terms (not verified line by line).
axes.fit: Fits: camera-controlled short films (preset camera language), creators outsourcing "director feel" to presets, dynamic social-media material. Does not fit: open weights, scenarios sensitive to mainland direct connection (direct 200 works but the product targets overseas), a long-narrative-consistency focus.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to creative products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **Camera-preset tracking quality on complex subjects (multiple people / fast motion)**
- **Style differences across vendors' outputs in the aggregated model list**
- **Conflict behavior between preset camera moves and custom prompts**
unknowns:
- The registered entity and team background (no official statement verified)
- The boundary list between in-house and aggregated models (not inventoried item by item)
- The training-use switch (not verified line by line)
- Cross-session memory mechanism (no official statement verified)
related: Both camera-oriented: Runway gives a professional toolchain to tune yourself, Higgsfield gives presets to apply in one click.
Both camera-move narrative oriented: Luma does first/last-frame interpolation, Higgsfield a preset camera-move library.
Kling also has a camera-control line: on Kling it is one feature inside a comprehensive big bench, Higgsfield's whole site revolves around it.
Image-to-video upstream: Higgsfield's input frames are often first drawn on Krea/Flux-style image benches before generation.
